newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks close up in flying finish.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks close up in flying finish.

text.p: SPI futures 2346 +45 US 30yr cl 6.88 -0.04
*Shares close higher on a flood of afternoon buying interest after futures surged. Turnover 361.54 million shares valued at A$1.05 bln, 976 stocks traded, 319 steady, 396 rises, 261 falls

Australian shares stormed home to their highest close in five months on Wednesday as a flood of afternoon buying interest, inspired by surging share price index futures, pushed turnover above the A$1 billion mark.
At 4.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 29.1 points higher at 2,314.6.
The December share price index futures contract was up 45 points at 2,346, a 31.4 point premium to the underlying index.
After muddling about for most of the day, buyers emerged in the afternoon and bid the banks higher again and pulled the major miners off their lows.
"It was on fire," said Greg Mathews, executive director of Australian equities at Mercantile Mutual.
"And it was led by the banks and TNT after the takeover,"
In the banks, Commonwealth Bank instalment receipts jumped four percent, highlighting their role as investor's Commonwealth Bank security of choice.
"You get a lot more bang for your buck with the receipts," Mathews said.
Pointing to the afternoon impetus received from the futures market, Mathews suggested some investors had been cashed up at the close of the September quarter and needed an outlet.
"There was too much cash on the sidelines after the end of the September quarter and with our market cheap relative to bonds, traders bought into the market via the SPI," he said.

Transport and logistics group TNT was the day's feature, its shares driven up about 50 percent after Dutch Telecom group Koninklijke PTT Nederland announced a A$2.45 a share agreed takeover bid, valuing TNT at about A$2 billion.
Fellow transport and logistics operators Brambles and Mayune Nickless also saw solid gains after the TNT bid with brokers saying the sector was being rerated.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 33 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade saw high levels of activity as traders bought the broader market while options trade received a boost from the increased buyer interest.
Total options traded 56,033 (44,789)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 9,816 (6,582)

In other local markets, Australian bonds closed at their strongest levels since March 1994, while the short end also finished up but well below its early highs after the Reserve Bank of Australia left interest rates unchanged.
By 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.72 percent, down 0.07 from Tuesday's close.
The Australian dollar sprang ahead Wednesday, capturing a four-year high on the yen after fears of an imminent rate cut were salved by Reserve Bank silence.
Speculation had been rife the central bank would ease policy this morning following its monthly board meeting on Tuesday, but the normal window for a move came and went with no announcement.
By 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), the local currency was quoted at US$0.7955/60.
